Does not work as direct replacement for WR17X11939RC. As others reported, the shoulders on the shaft are too high, so it cannot be reassembled correctly. Luckily I have a Dremel and was able to modify it, but not all others will.
Like some of the other reviews, the shaft had to be ground to increase the depth of the “flat” spot on the sides to allow the parts to slide on fully.

Even though the Amazon ad says this is an exact fit for a WR 17x1139 auger, it really wasn't. The threaded shaft with a flat flange to hold the metal retaining washers was about a quarter inch shorter than the original part from my refrigerator. Several reviews recommended grinding the shaft to make it about a quarter of an inch longer for holding the 2 fixed blades, 3 rotating blades and the original number of nylon washers. That is completely unnecessary. Since this auger replaces so many different models, not all were an EXACT fit, but it can easily be made to fit and work without grinding the shaft. It turns out that the thickness of one flat nylon washer is exactly the same thickness as the length of the shaft to the flat flange is short. By eliminating 1 flat nylon washer, the Auger can be made to work perfectly. Another important point to pay attention to is that the 3 rotating blades have a single digit number stamped into each of them. Mine were 7, 8 & 9. It is important to keep these in numerical order so that they progressively and evenly advance to crush the ice.

I wish I had taken a picture of my final configuration, but the sequence of blades and washers went like this:
1. Two metal Slotted washers against the flange
2. Rotating blade #7 with the numbered side down toward the metal washers
3. Dual diameter nylon washer with the larger diameter portion against blade 7 & the smaller diameter being inserted into the first statio

Let me start by saying, I didn't care if my dispenser worked, i can open my freezer, and get ice out myself.  That being said, I ordered this after seeing that it is basically the only auger available.  Mine is a chromed steel auger, which was the problem.  The chrome had started coming off, and there was rust bits all in the ice bin.  The ice maker itself works fine.  I got this auger, and it came quickly.  First thing I noticed, was that mine was a regular thread nylon nut, not reverse thread, like the videos show.  No biggie, it's a plastic nut, I'll make it reverse thread...  No problems all assembled, then I thought about it, and looked at the two augers, and figured out why.  My auger/motor spins the opposite direction, so it won't dispense ice,  but I don't care about that.  Bottom line, if your auger is metal, it's  probably reverse direction of this.  But, if you just don't want ice to fall out the hole, and don't want rust in your ice, this works great!!

The auger looks very well designed, and feels identical to the auger I removed from our GE refridgerator. The installation is not real difficult, the tricky part is putting the grinding blades BACK on when installing the new auger.

TAKE A PICTURE of the old unit, BEFORE you DISASSEMBLE it. Also when disassembling make note of the direction of each WHITE washer.

BEFORE STARTING THE REPLACEMENT PROCESS NOTE THE THREADED END OF THE OLD UNIT vs. THE NEW UNIT. THERE IS A FLAT SURFACE JUST BEFORE THE THREADS THAT HAS TO BE IDENTICAL. IF NOT IDENTICAL YOU HAVE TO "GRIND" it down. Otherwise, all the washers will not go back on.

Suggestion -- have a rod shaped item (I think that a common old school type pencil) to move the blades to as a GROUP. Keeping them in order, will make your job easier., would work. THIS IS... the hardest part of replacing the auger.

Good luck!!

The fin on my refrigerator ice auger closest to the dispenser broke off & it was taking what seemed like forever to dispense ice, can't have that!  So I went searching for a new one only to find out that my 2018 GE GSE25HMHJHES refrigerator specs show that I have to buy the whole ice bucket assembly at $200+, can't have that either!  The WR17X11705 seemed to be the solution & things were going smoothly until I started comparing shafts & like other reviews the top of shaft is @ 3/16" longer. I chose to grind down the shaft with a dremel tool & all went back together & works great. I do like 'Golf Nut's idea about removing washer, sounds like it would work & might be a lot easier than the grinding method. So don't be afraid it won't work or can't be altered, buy it & you can make it work!

Ended up substituting other spacers in order to ensure length of replacement auger ended up being the same as original part and would fit properly back into housing.  Threaded and tapered end of auger shaft need to be redesigned to ensure original blades, spacers and end cap can be re-used and will fit properly.

There are also a lot of air pockets in the plastic auger screw. I added some pictures of those too.

Total installation time was about an hour because I had to uninstall and then re-install after realizing that I forgot to knock out the tab for the water fill vinyl tube.
1. Do not disassemble ANYTHING from the old unit before you get your new one. You will have to use every removable part from your old one on this newer unit. I guess that helps them keep the cost down.
2. The most important item that LUCKILY I saved was the wiring harness that connects the unit to the freezer. If you had thrown that out, then you would have been really out of luck. It would not be easy to find a replacement.
3. You will need the clips that hold that wiring harness to the unit, and the screws that screw the clip onto the unit.
4. You will need to keep your original metal bracket that helps support the front end of the unit. The plastic piece that they shipped would now fit in my configuration. Luckily I had not scrapped my bracket, although I did have to go retrieve it out of my metal recycle bucket in the garage.
5. The metal bail wire that tells the unit the the ice bucket if full was not clicked into the motor end I had to push it in. I do not know if that affected the fact that it does not "freely" swing like the old unit did, but if your unit does not make ice, then you have to manually reach in and pull the bail wire down so that the unit knows there is room to dump the ice. After a couple of weeks, it seems to be working ok though. Also it is a single wire ver
